title: North Korea Is More Dangerous Than You Think
summary: Explainer on why North Korea deters attack: artillery aimed at Seoul, nuclear missiles, cybertheft, its alliance with Russia and three paths ahead.

assertions.quote: The fear isn't that North Korea could win a war. It's that it has made sure nobody can afford to fight one.

verdicts.note: No state has attacked North Korea since 1953, and studies of a second Korean war project very heavy early losses in Seoul.

assertions.quote: Flown on a normal path, analysts calculated, it could reach any city in the continental United States.

verdicts.note: Hwasong-15 and later tests show ICBM range, but reliable re-entry of a warhead has not been demonstrated.

assertions.quote: researchers estimate it has around sixty assembled warheads, and the material for more.

verdicts.note: SIPRI and FAS estimate about 50 assembled warheads with material for more.
SIPRI estimates North Korea has possibly assembled around 60 warheads, with fissile material for at least 30 more and accelerating production.

assertions.quote: In tests since 1999, it has hit its target twelve times out of twenty-one.

verdicts.note: Ground-based interceptor tests succeed only about half the time under scripted conditions against a single target.
The Bulletin calls missile defence at best only partially effective; a general judgment, not specific to a North Korean ICBM.

assertions.quote: A 2020 RAND study modeled about three hundred of them firing at Seoul for one hour, with no warning

verdicts.note: Studies such as RAND's 2020 estimate tens of thousands of casualties in the first hour, though the video's millions-in-a-day figure is an older, higher estimate.

assertions.quote: around eleven thousand North Korean soldiers were fighting for Russia in Kursk

verdicts.note: Confirmed by South Korean, Ukrainian and US intelligence and later acknowledged by Moscow and Pyongyang.

assertions.quote: a White House official estimated that stolen crypto funded about half of the missile program.

verdicts.note: The FBI attributed the 2025 Bybit theft to North Korea, and UN experts link cyber revenue to weapons funding.

EFIS says North Korea funds its weapons programmes mainly through more than 100,000 overseas workers and covert IT firms (nearly half a billion euros a year), plus extortion, rather than describing cybertheft.
US intelligence says North Korean cryptocurrency heists and other financial crimes net at least $1 billion a year to fund the regime's weapons programs.

assertions.quote: To North Korea, the bomb isn't a bargaining chip. It's life insurance.

verdicts.note: It wrote its nuclear status into the constitution in 2023 and every disarmament deal since 1994 has collapsed.

assertions.quote: In recent polls, between six and eight in ten South Koreans say their country should build its own.

verdicts.note: Repeated polls since 2022 find roughly 70 percent support for an indigenous South Korean arsenal.

assertions.quote: Which leaves the third, and most likely, path. Nothing changes.

verdicts.note: The armistice has held for over seventy years and neither side gains from starting a war.
Polymarket priced a North Korean invasion of South Korea before 2027 at 5.5%, consistent with a continued standoff without war in the near term.
